name: Jagannātha Purī
aka: Jagannatha Puri, Puri, Purī, Śrīkṣetra, Srikshetra, Nīlācala, Nilacala, Puruṣottama-kṣetra, Purushottam, Śaṅkha-kṣetra
location: On the sea shore, in Utkala (Orissa)
about:
Also called Śrīkṣetra, Nīlācala and Puruṣottama: the place of the pastimes of Śrī Jagannātha, where Kṛṣṇa is present as Dāru-brahma. Being shaped like a conch it is called Śaṅkha-kṣetra; according to the Utkala-khaṇḍa the kṣetra measures five kroś, of which the two along the sea are the holiest. Mahārāja Indradyumna first brought Śrī Nīlamādhava to light; under King Anaṅgabhīma-deva the kṣetra was fully adorned and the present temple was built (some 40–50 lakh rupees), and he gave much land for the offerings and festivals. In Mahāprabhu's time Rāja Pratāparudra ruled.
The temple has four gates: the Siṁha-dvāra (east), Aśva-dvāra (south), Khañja-dvāra (west) and Hasti-dvāra (north); near it the Akṣaya-vaṭa, Vimalā and Lakṣmī.
Śrī Caitanya lived at Purī and became the glory of Śrīkṣetra and all Orissa; in the Gambhīrā, in the mood of Rādhā, he showed the pastimes told in the Caitanya-caritāmṛta.
Festivals: the Snāna on Jyaiṣṭha pūrṇimā; Rathayātrā on Āṣāḍha śukla dvitīyā (the day before, the Guṇḍicā-mārjana, «a duty, a joy and a remembrance for the followers of Gaura»; for nine days Jagannātha, Baladeva, Subhadrā and Sudarśana stay in the Guṇḍicā temple, and on the ninth comes the return); Śayana on Āṣāḍha śukla ekādaśī; Jhūlana on Śrāvaṇa pūrṇimā; Pārśva-parivartana; Utthāna on Kārtika śukla ekādaśī; Prāvaraṇa; Puṣyābhiṣeka; the Māgha festival; Dola on Phālguna pūrṇimā; Damanaka-bhañjana; and twenty-one days of Candana-yātrā from Vaiśākha śukla tṛtīyā.
The best-known Gauḍīya maṭhas: Ṭoṭā-gopīnātha, Nārāyaṇa-chātā, the samādhi-maṭha of Haridāsa Ṭhākura, Bāli-maṭha, Nandinī-maṭha, Sātāsana, Rādhākānta-maṭha (the Gambhīrā), Siddha-bakula, Gaṅgāmātā-maṭha, Jhāñjapiṭhā-maṭha and Kuñja-maṭha. Tīrthas: the five tīrthas (Cakra-tīrtha, Svarga-dvāra, Śveta-gaṅgā, Mārkaṇḍeya and Indradyumna-sarovara), Narendra-sarovara, Āṭhāra-nālā, Yameśvara Śiva, Lokanātha and Kapālamocana Mahādeva. On the way to Lokanātha is Purī Gosāñi's well (Caitanya-bhāgavata Antya 3.235–258).

name: Gambhīrā
about:
The Gambhīrā, in the Rādhākānta-maṭha, one of the Gauḍīya maṭhas of Purī. While staying in the Gambhīrā Mahāprabhu was at every moment overwhelmed by the mood of Śrī Rādhā; the sweetness of those pastimes is told in the Caitanya-caritāmṛta and other books.
The biographies in the library add: the Gambhīrā was a solitary room in the house of Kāśī Miśra, the guru of King Pratāparudra; after Mahāprabhu, Vakreśvara Paṇḍita lived there and his disciple Gopāla Guru Gosvāmī installed Śrī Śrī Rādhā-kānta.

name: Haridāsa Ṭhākura's samādhi
about: The samādhi-maṭha of Haridāsa Ṭhākura, one of the Gauḍīya maṭhas of Purī. Siddha-bakula is listed beside it among the maṭhas of Purī.

name: Ṭoṭā-gopīnātha
aka: Tota Gopinatha, Ṭoṭā, Tota, Caṭaka-parvata, Chataka parvata
location: At Ṭoṭā in Purī, near the Caṭaka-parvata, a sand hill on the sea shore
about:
Near the Caṭaka-parvata — a sand hill on the sea shore at Puruṣottama-kṣetra — is Ṭoṭā-gopīnātha, the deity served by Gadādhara Paṇḍita.
Ţoṭā village is the śrīpāṭa of Murāri Māhiti; Garuḍa Paṇḍita also lived here.

name: Guṇḍicā temple
about: Here Śrī Jagannātha rests for the nine days of the Rathayātrā. A home of the loving pastimes of Śrī Gaura; the day before the Rathayātrā is the Guṇḍicā-mārjana, the cleaning of the temple.

name: Narendra-sarovara
aka: Narendra sarovar, Narendra tank, Candana-pukur, Chandan pukur
location: About a mile north-east of the temple of Jagannātha
about: The «Candana-pukur» of Śrīkṣetra: 873 feet long and 743 wide. It is said that it was made in the 13th century by an officer called Narendra; others say Narendra Indradyumna had it dug for the Candana-yātrā of Śrī Puruṣottama. For the twenty-one days of the Candana-yātrā Jagannātha's festival image, Śrī Madana-mohana, enjoys boat pastimes on it. A place of the pastimes of Śrī Gaurāṅga, and where Gadādhara Paṇḍita Gosvāmī read the Śrīmad Bhāgavatam.

name: Ālālanātha
location: South of Purī, a mile from Beṇṭapura
about: During the fortnight when the deities of Jagannātha stay in the nirodhana-gṛha beside the jagamohana (the dayitās offer them medicine and sweets, saying Jagannātha has fever), Mahāprabhu used to go to see Ālālanātha.

name: Beṇṭapura
location: South of the road to Ālālanātha; Ālālanātha is a mile away

name: Kaṭaka
location: Between the Kāṭhajuḍī and the Mahānadī
about: The former capital and one of the chief towns of Orissa. Sākṣi-gopāla, brought from Vidyānagara by Śrī Puruṣottama-deva, was first installed at Kaṭaka, and here Śrī Gaurāṅga saw him. In the Mohammadiyā Bāzār quarter the Jagannātha-vallabha garden is known as Rāmānanda Rāya's; in 1312 sāl Nitāi-Gaura and Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa deities were installed there. There are also a deity of Jāhnavā Mātā and Gopeśvara Mahādeva.

name: Sākṣi-gopāla
location: At the village of Satyavādī, near Jagannātha Purī
about: The Gopāla who bore witness for the younger and the elder brāhmaṇa. He came first to the temple of Jagannātha and then to this village of Satyavādī. The temple stands in a garden called Gupta-vṛndāvana; the present building is said to be the work of Bābā Brahmacārī, the famous guru of the Marāṭhās. Near the bazar is a «Candana-pukur», where the Candana-yātrā of Sākṣi-gopāla's festival image is held.

name: Remuṇā
about:
The original deity of Kṣīra-corā Gopīnātha is at Remuṇā. Mādhavendra Purī left his body here, and his samādhi is here. The village goddess is Rāmacaṇḍī: it is said that Śrī Rāmacandra and Sītā worshipped her, and that on their way back from Laṅkā they stayed four days at Remuṇā, where Rāma shot seven arrows to bring a stream of pure water for Sītā's bath.
Āramaṇī, about three miles west of Remuṇā: in its «Anantasāgara» tank the servants hid Śrī Gopīnātha for fear of Kālāpāhāḍ.

name: Jājapura
location: On the bank of the Vaitaraṇī, in Utkala
about: The tīrtha of Nābhi-gayā in Virajā-kṣetra. The temple of Ādivarāha, with Yajña-varāha and Śveta-varāha — three forms; the temple of Jagannātha on the Vaitaraṇī; Nābhi-gayā, where piṇḍa is offered in a well (said to be on the navel of Gayāsura). Its glories are told in the Mahābhārata (Vana-parva), the Brahma-purāṇa and the Kapila-saṁhitā. The name is said to come from the Śaiva king Yayāti Keśarī («Yayātipura»). Sanctified by the feet of Śrī Gaura (Caitanya-bhāgavata Antya 2).
